patterns.pattern: Bounded lookahead waypoints with shrink/replan recovery
patterns.observed: Route selects a lookahead cell, trims unreachable or excessive-deviation candidates, and decreases its step size when position stops changing.
patterns.proposal: Implement a pure conservative waypoint selector over our public geometry: initially coalesce only constant-direction path runs, cap lookahead, stop at first warp trigger, and reject blocked/corner-cutting cells. Track requested endpoint and received baseline per agent. Keep the current fresh actual-position arrival predicate and paced bounded retries; never interpret a simulated path, pos_to, elapsed walk time, or send success as arrival. A separate bounded replan from a new observed position may shorten future segments; missing receipts still fail closed.
patterns.tradeoffs: Fewer movement commands, but server-selected paths and unknown portal triggers can make long segments unsafe. Keep one-cell fallback unless pinned server route semantics and trigger catalogs validate the run. Do not adopt OpenKore predicted-position completion or teleport recovery.
acceptance_tests: Open straight corridor chooses capped multi-cell endpoint; bent/diagonal obstacle route truncates before corner.
First trigger tile ends segment; no waypoint after trigger.
A fresh 0087 with from!=to does not clear pending; stale seq and fabricated elapsed arrival do not clear pending.
Fresh matching actual from==to clears pending; retry pacing and limit remain unchanged; epoch/map changes invalidate segment state.
Visible blockers belong only to this agent; two instances never share pending state.

patterns.pattern: Persistent target identity, paced attacks, receipt-driven progress timeout
patterns.observed: Attack retains queued target IDs, stops on disappearance, checks give-up bounds, and refreshes inactivity timing on damage/miss/skill changes.
patterns.proposal: Introduce an instance-owned CombatSession(target_id, epoch, last_command_at, last_progress_seq, deadline) with an injected clock. Lock one eligible visible target rather than switching whenever nearest ordering changes; cancel on observed disappearance/death, goal interruption, rest or epoch change. Gate ordinary attacks by a policy interval; only fresh matching observed damage renews progress, not another request. Route into a pinned-mechanics range when necessary. Keep explicit inactivity and total-session caps.
patterns.tradeoffs: A target lock needs interruption rules and may prefer a less convenient target. Command pacing is a policy guard, not an invented attack-speed measurement; native range/weapon mechanics must come from our compiled server.
acceptance_tests: Nearest actor order swaps without changing locked target.
Repeated calls before injected-clock interval produce no second wire attack.
Only own-AID/locked-target new damage renews inactivity; another actor damage or duplicate seq does not.
No progress reaches timeout, target disappearance cancels, and death/epoch/transport gap blocks further commands.
No cross-agent combat state.

patterns.pattern: Visible-floor loot selection with acquisition receipts and bounded failure memory
patterns.observed: Take has a target ID, timeout/failure marker, standing and movement gates, and request pacing. Auto-gather filters failed/young/excluded items and nearby players/portals; proximity is a heuristic, not an ownership proof.
patterns.proposal: Remove the bag-inventory-as-loot-availability condition. Use an explicit per-agent visible-floor perception seam, select a permitted floor ID, stand/approach, then keep one pending pickup with injected-clock pacing and a timeout. Count success only from a new positive acquisition receipt; floor disappearance alone is not acquisition. Remember bounded failed IDs within the current epoch/map and expire/reset them. Require an explicit ownership policy based on available receipts/configuration; never invent owner fields absent from our wire view.
patterns.tradeoffs: Our pickup receipt contains item/index/amount, not floor ID, so serialized attempts improve correlation but do not prove exclusive causality against concurrent acquisition. Empty bag and floor visibility are separate facts. Unknown ownership must stay unknown; OpenKore proximity rules are insufficient proof.
acceptance_tests: Empty bag plus permitted visible floor item produces a pickup path; full bag with no floor does not request Loot.
Two ticks before deadline emit one pickup request.
Removal packet without successful positive receipt never increments acquired count.
Failure/timeout cools down only that floor ID; another eligible item can proceed.
Unknown ownership is denied or explicitly operator-policy allowed; epoch and map reset clear stale candidates; two bots remain isolated.

patterns.pattern: Separate public inter-map plan from current-map movement and warp-wait execution
patterns.observed: CalcMapRoute is a calculation task separate from traversal. MapRoute holds a map solution, clears leg state on map changes, and enters a warp-wait substage.
patterns.proposal: Generalize StarterRoute into public PortalEdge and instance-owned PortalJourney(current_leg, approach, expected_destination, receipt_baseline, deadline). Use a bounded graph search over the pinned owned-world public warp catalog, route to first trigger entry, wait for an actual matching native transition before advancing, and handle unexpected received maps by replanning or explicit failure. Preserve the already repaired mapLoadEndAck lifecycle; do not add a second ACK producer.
patterns.tradeoffs: Costs, conditional NPCs and same-map warps require pinned server-specific metadata. Initial vertical should use deterministic walking warps only, no transport items, commands or inferred transitions.
acceptance_tests: Two-map fixture stops at trigger and sends no destination-map moves until fresh matching transition.
Wrong-map and stale transition cannot advance expected leg.
Warp wait times out explicitly; same-map warp requires receipt plus expected destination coordinates.
No actor or floor state survives a map transition; ACK regression stays green.

patterns.pattern: Rest hysteresis and observed-leader follow bands
patterns.observed: SitAuto uses lower/upper HP/SP thresholds and aggression, weight and skill gates. Follow moves beyond a maximum separation toward a minimum separation and resets routes when the leader moves.
patterns.proposal: Add instance-owned recovery mode: enter below a configured low HP threshold, stay resting through the middle band, leave only above a higher threshold and after observed standing. Keep survival interrupts and compiled-server sit prerequisites. Follow/support is a later separate controller over this agent received party/player observations, with min/max distance bands and loss timeout; catalogued skills do not prove current ownership or cooldown.
patterns.tradeoffs: Hysteresis avoids repeated rest/attack switching, but aggression and unknown vitals need fail-closed policies. Rest can fail to regenerate under pinned mechanics; timeout/escalation must avoid an infinite wait. Do not import global player knowledge.
acceptance_tests: HP below low enters rest; HP between bands does not attack; high HP begins observed stand recovery.
Unknown vitals, attack interruption and epoch reset do not claim recovery.
Follow stays still within band, replans only from received leader movement, and stops on leader loss.
Equipment recovery is deferred until inventory/equipment confirmations exist; do not infer equip success from a request.
